olivia_cs: ACME reported a steady stream of 429s starting ~08:12 UTC. Their average qps is low (~0.25 r/s) but we see short bursts ~250-320 reqs/min that coincide with customer cron + a fanout job. They sent logs: `2026-03-15T08:12:31Z -> 429 X-RateLimit-Limit:100 X-RateLimit-Remaining:0` and a note that they use our Node SDK v2 with HTTP/2 streaming enabled. Can eng help triage? :eyes:
maria_support: Thanks — do we have the customer's org_id and which model/route they hit? Any SDK version + region?

olivia_cs: Org: acme-corp-42, route: /v1/chat/completions (model: redwood-gptx-3-large), SDK: node@2.4.1, region: us-west-2. They said retries were immediate (no jitter). Attached a small repro trace (snippet).
sam_eng: Quick thought: if their client spawns many concurrent streams on one HTTP/2 connection you can get short wall-clock bursts even if avg qps is low. Also: streaming-enabled clients sometimes keep many inflight requests open which interacts poorly with our per-minute buckets. Can you paste their minimal repro?
olivia_cs: Pasted snippet from customer:
```
for (let i=0;i<120;i++) fetch('/v1/chat/completions',{method:'POST', body:payload})
```
They run that job every minute from several hosts. No jitter/backoff.
sam_eng: Ok that's classic fanout spike. Two immediate actions: 1) verify whether those bursts align with our per-minute window boundaries (we use sliding 60s buckets in edge limiter). 2) recommend client-side exponential backoff + jitter; if they need steady throughput recommend batching requests or moving that job to a slower cadence. Example backoff snippet for Node SDK:
```
await retry(async ()=> client.chat.create(...), {retries:5, minTimeout:100, factor:2, randomize:true})
```
nishi_sre: I'm pulling edge limiter logs now for acme-corp-42 between 2026-03-15T08:10:00Z and 08:20:00Z. If we see many short spikes we can correlate to edge pod CPU/queue saturation. Also checking if they hit any per-tenant slot caps (we have a default inflight cap of 50).
ingest-bot: deploy-bot: FYI a config tweak to per-minute smoothing was deployed 2026-03-14 22:05 UTC (PR #4281).
maria_support: Olivia — please ask ACME to enable jitter + a small random delay across hosts and to collect client-side timestamps for a 2-minute run so we can map events to our logs. Also ask if they can temporarily reduce concurrency to confirm root cause.
olivia_cs: Sent guidance and sample backoff + jitter code. Customer will run an instrumented job in ~20m and share logs.
sam_eng: In parallel I'll run a query on edge-rate limiter for that org and a trace query for the model route. If pattern matches fanout -> recommend soft quota bump (temporary) or suggest dedicated rate-limited pool for their cron jobs.
nishi_sre: Query results: saw three 30s windows at 08:12:30-08:13:00 where effective per-minute rate exceeded 280 RPM and Remaining dropped to 0. Edge CPU briefly high on pod edge-24. Filing follow-up ops ticket to add mitigation rule: auto-shed non-streaming cron bursts if they exceed X.
maria_support: Thanks — keep me posted. If customer confirms jitter fixes it we'll close. If not, escalate to account exec for quota/packaging discussion. :thumbsup
